decide what to ask people to meet it. Nobody will correct you; whatever you write goes out.

OBJECTIVE: Figure out the best event to put on for the Columbia AI Club next spring
AUDIENCE: Columbia undergraduates interested in AI

Design a short survey that would actually settle this objective. Between 5 and 8 questions.
Prefer multiple choice and rating scales over free text, because you must analyse the answers
yourself afterwards. Include at least one open question so you can learn something you did
not think to ask about. Do not ask for names or contact details.

Reply with JSON only, no prose outside it:
{
  "reasoning": "<2-3 sentences: what has to be true for the objective to be met, and what you
                therefore need to find out>",
  "title": "<short survey title>",
  "questions": [{"text": "<question>", "type": "single|multi|scale|open", "options": ["..."]}],
  "success_looks_like": "<one sentence: what pattern in the answers would give you a clear answer>"
}

args.brief:
Create a survey titled "Columbia AI Club — Spring Event Planning Survey".
It exists to answer this objective: Figure out the best event to put on for the Columbia AI Club next spring

Use exactly these questions, in this order:
1. [single] Which of the following best describes your current involvement with AI? (Select one) Options: I'm casually curious — I follow AI news but don't build things yet / I'm learning — taking courses or working through tutorials / I'm actively building — personal projects, research, or internships / I work on AI professionally or in a research lab.
2. [multi] What would you most want to get out of an AI Club spring event? (Select up to 2) Options: Learn a concrete technical skill I can use right away / Meet other students who are into AI / Get exposure to real-world AI applications or research / Hear from industry professionals or researchers / Work on something with a team (hackathon / build session) / Get feedback on a project I'm already working on.
3. [single] Which event format appeals to you most for a spring event? (Select one) Options: Full-day hackathon / Half-day workshop with hands-on coding / Panel discussion with Q&A (industry / research speakers) / Demo showcase — students present their AI projects / Networking mixer with lightning talks / Speaker series (one or two keynote talks).
4. [scale] How likely would you be to attend each of the following formats if the AI Club hosted one this spring? (Rate each 1 = Very unlikely → 5 = Very likely) Options: Full-day hackathon / Half-day hands-on workshop / Speaker panel / Q&A / Student project demo day / Networking mixer with lightning talks.
5. [single] What day and time works best for you? (Select one) Options: Weekday evening (6 pm – 9 pm) / Saturday daytime (10 am – 4 pm) / Sunday daytime (10 am – 4 pm) / No strong preference.
6. [multi] What would most likely stop you from attending an AI Club event? (Select up to 2) Options: Conflict with coursework / exams / Event feels too advanced for my skill level / Event feels too basic for my skill level / Don't know anyone else attending / Event is too long / Lack of tangible outcome (certificate, project, prize, etc.).
7. [open] Is there an AI topic, format, or guest speaker type that you wish the Columbia AI Club would do — but haven't seen yet? Tell us anything we might have missed.

Keep it short and plain. Do not add demographic questions I have not asked for.
Publish it as soon as it is ready.
